lots.guide_summary: Mostly SOLD: five single verandah panels at Gowans in Aug-Sep 2026 made $25 to $220 hammer (two of those with 0 bids, so soft). Category SOLD guides: a pair of tall panels $675 and a stack of matching Adelaide balustrade panels $3,800. ASKING: SA dealer wants $200 to $240 a panel ($960 for four). No UNSOLD found. All AUD.
lots.working: No sold set of four found, so values are scaled from single-panel Gowans sales (close, not same). Keep: lowest single SOLD $25 x 4 panels = $100; $100 / 1.22 = $81.97, round down to $80. Flip: likely Tasmanian resale about $50 a panel from the $30-$70 bid-supported singles, so 4 x $50 = $200; less about 20% auction seller fees ($40) and $0 postage (bulky, local pickup sale) = $160; $160 / 2.44 = $65.57, round down to $65. A buyer restoring a verandah would pay well above this (dealer $240 each), which is the upside, not the bid basis.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification as cast iron rests on the title only (could be aluminium reproduction), no maker mark, and the SOLD evidence is single panels of different designs, scaled up to four.
lots.condition: Appear complete with feet and top rails, painted green, no obvious breaks visible at this resolution. Paint over possible rust; one panel is a different design so only three form a matching run.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo against a roller door. Three panels share an arched top with star or flower motifs, the third from left is a different design with an oval lower frame. Lugs at top corners and feet at the base, typical of balustrade panels. No foundry mark visible.
lots.question_for_armitage: Are these genuine cast iron (heavy, magnet sticks) or aluminium reproductions? Any cracks, broken lugs or welded repairs? Please confirm sizes.
